column1: # Open gaps (tools/bench.sh): a shortfall that is known and not yet closed. One line per gap, tabs between:
# linux: the metric misses its target against Linux's locked number (bench/reference.tsv); the bound is the
# ratio to that number it may not exceed. ratchet: it is worse than its own best (bench/ratchet.tsv); the bound
# is the value it may not pass, on the host named ("-": any host, a count). While a metric is no worse than its
# bound a run reports it OPEN and passes; past it, ERROR. A line is added by a commit that says why, tightened
# or removed by `bench.sh --update-ratchet`, and never loosened. No milestone is declared over a line of a
# metric it requires. Each line is work owed: close it in Silica, or decide the cost and move its ratchet with
# The bounds below are from the sessions of 2026-11-22 (the single-processor and device values from a session
# that had a stray process on one measured core, which those paths do not use: tighten them from the first

the tail went from 6.2 to 9.2 us since the ratchet was set; the cause is not attributed (bench.sh --compare over the kernel commits since would name it)

11 instructions a round trip since the ratchet was set (994.7), named by bench.sh --compare 6f6c470..61c6aff --only insns --steps: +9 at c0cc6f9 (a receive listening on a notification: the new test in ReplyRecv and the spills around it; its own measurement found the time unchanged, 413 against 415 ns), +2 at 6e0ee56 (the timer's scheduler fix, +1 on a context switch too). To win back in the ReplyRecv fast path's register use, not by dropping the listen

35 instructions a fault since the ratchet was set (2766.3), named by the same run: +52 at fd1d99e (device address spaces: the mapping path's dispatch), -19 at c0cc6f9 (device mapping moved off the fault path; check_map, slot_in and leaf inlined again), +2 at 6e0ee56. The rest is register allocation around the inlined table walk (c0cc6f9's message: the old body beside the device copy measured 2794). 2026-11-22: 2807.4, past this bound (the gate is red): SignalRecv (one kernel entry for a wake-up and a wait) cost 16 at 1cdb520, of which moving it into a call of its own won back 10; to be weighed by timing blk_read4k_qd1 with and without it once the desktop is idle, and taken out if it does not win. bench.sh cannot yet do that comparison: --compare and --sweep build variants of the kernel's benchmark image only and skip the system image's blk_* and net_* metrics; a --sweep reaching the system build (libsys reading SILICA_TUNE_SIGNAL_RECV) is the instrument owed
